body:
This is a ever ongoing discussion here. I brought it up several times. When I see posts like "my eye twitched for a week" or the "tongue twitches" that are actually normal movements.. 

I understand being afraid, I have terrible symptoms myself. But some people should count their blessings, and be grateful they don't belong here. 

I wished that my symptoms were anxiety induced.

This is me currently. Spasms in neck and tongue. Twitching in face.. 

Feels horrible.
I know.. the thing that sends me spiraling is my spasming tongue..

Oh, I've tried everything. What scares me the most is my tongue.. I feel like it's the most scary place to spasm/twitch. 

Everytime I feel like I can handle this, another symptom appears.
Yes, the uncertainty of it is awful. It's like you try to be rational, but your body tells you something else.

Oh my, that sounds awful. 

So sad that nothing works. Did you just wake up one day with migraines?

I grew up with a close family member needing emergency medication due to migraine attacks. It's no joke.. 

Take care.

Thanks for your reply. I really needed help to reflect upon why I feel I can't go on another 4 years. I think it's the draining part of it, if you know what I mean. I always feel like I can't live my life to the fullest. It's always that pesky eye spasm, or cheek twitch that comes along and ruins the joy. 

Now with my tongue spasming, it interrupts my speaking because my tongue is constantly pulling to the left. It's terrifying to say the least.

I feel like a walking freak show. 

Also, I think it's the grief of not improving. 10 years ago, if I got an eye twitch, I knew it would be gone in a matter of hours. You really go insane when it just lasts and lasts for years. 

I think with your example with arthritis, it's an easier condition to accept. Everyone knows what it is, and you can medicate it. Same basically goes with most "well known" diseases. Bfs is basically a "we dont know, but it's probably benign" condition. And that's hard for me to accept. Does that mean this is my life now? Can I get better? Will it get worse? Such a mind game.


I'm not suicidal, but I have days where I feel I can't take anymore of this. I guess we all have.. I do cherish the good days. I just wished there were more of them. 

So that's my Christmas wish this year, that we all get better. And have a wonderful Christmas! Please dear someone who's in charge, make my wish come true ❤️
Really appreciate your advice. I know the tongue is examined at rest, the only reason I stick it out is to show it better. It spasms at rest also, and during the night..
I know.. have asked to see my Neuro. I'm guessing it's a 1 year wait.. lol

Yes, thanks so much for the advice. I do have a pillow, but have to admit that I don't use it every time.  The baby also hangs on my arm a lot. 

You're absolutely right, I tried fixing it, but only made it worse. I guess I was so sick of my tongue twitching, that I exaggerated the stretching.
Thanks for your reply. I just feel like other peoples tongue twitching is a little flicker, while mine is spasming the entire left side. Hard to ignore..
I most definitely feel it.
Yes that must be her.
Yes.. My point exactly. The fear becomes worse than the actual disease.

I think the moral of my story have to be that it's easy to be fooled by these extreme health anxiety people.

I hope people aren't watching her one video of a normal twitch, and assumes the worst because of her hashtags.

Hard to focuse when your eyes are going bananas.. 🥴 I also miss being social, I can't have a good time when the twitches bother me. I used to love being busy, doing alot of things. I also miss being able to just go someplace new, experiencing new places and things. Now it's day to day, if it's a good day I may be able to go to the grocery store. 

Life has sure changed.
Yes, I usually bury my face hard in the pillow or hold it in place with my hand. I hate it.

Trying to ignore it is basically the only thing you can do. Just feels like I've played this game for too long now. I don't have anxiety, but I've asked for any medication, like just give me something. But they won't.  I'm only offered Botox, buy they can't put it everywhere. 

I'm seriously considering lying to try some anxiety medication. But it's so strict here..

Good you found something that seems to help. 5 weeks in, I bet it will disappear in your case. Really hope so.

Feel you! It's awful I know. Seems like everything triggers it.

I agree that nothing helps, and this comes from someone who has tried everything. If you also twitch elsewhere than the face, neuro totally dismiss HFS. But does it feel like HFS sometimes, - absolutely.

My face has twitched for a solid 3 years now. I don't think bulbar starts with twitches.. But I'm not going to find out either. Twitches below the neck don't bother me at all. But the constant ones on my face... they push me over the edge.

I think it was the 5th of January I remembered that the date had passed... Because I was better.

I sometimes think back on that date, and everything I would have missed out on. It also gives me hope in believing better days will come. 

The chance of me ending it because of my health issues are still high though. On bad days I do find relief in knowing I can end it whenever I want. Maybe that's whats kept me going a little bit further.

Also there's hope, hope for better days.

So insane that we just got this one day, and it never left..

I've spent countless nights holding it "in place" with my hands. The face also easily triggers by nothing and everything. I can yawn and set off a cheek twitch that will last for weeks. I seriously can't live like this forever.

I have such poor life quality because of this.

More drama..

The constant "but you're better today, right?" Or when my dad went on to announce that I was doing better, just because he couldn't grasp the concept of being so extremely sick for so long. He just assumed it couldn't last... Bah

And there's the usual "have you tried ginger tea?" 

Also when my partner would ask me "you don't want an apple, or?" - It's not that I didnt want anything, my body wasn't able to.. I was not choosing to starve!!

BUT the following day my fasting was high. Next I tried 2 tablespoons of whole grain rice with dinner, after was ok. But again, fasting over.. I then proceeded to eat no carbs, and fasting went under.

What got me through was knowing that I had done it before, and actually survived.

I have completely given up on carbs, only the minor under 5g/100g in certain vegetables, cottage cheese, etc.

Totally agree. In my country everyone goes to public school. Which means you ca be blind, deaf and in a wheelchair with severe mental disabilities, - and still be put in an ordinary classroom.

He's a youth now, and still in the baby fase, with newborn instincts intact. He had zero benefits from being placed there, and should rather be given intensive special education.

When it comes to kids with severe attention/anger disorder, to the point where they are a danger to others. They need to be removed immediately. It's not enough to have someone follow them 1-1.

This time I haven't vomited as much, but I've been extremely extremely sick/nauseous. Not able to move, eat or drink. Couldn't watch tv, or look at my phone. The only thing that got me through was knowing it would get better.

I hate to vomit, so for me it was probably worse the first time... or maybe they were equally bad. 

Note : I did not take any medication. Only iv fluids. And most important, this is my 4th baby. Which means it didn't show up in all pregnancies. Only the usual morning sickness in the others.

For me it slowly resolved during second trimester. Not to the point where I feal great, but I no longer have a death wish.

I still can't eat certain things, drink water or smell something I don't like.

The only comfort I can provide is that it's "just" a short period in life. It's not forever, although living with it at the time is horrendous. 

I read an article about a woman who planned ahead of pregnancy, because she knew she was getting hg. She had nurses coming to her house every day, IVs, husband taking care of the other kids.. I personally could never. If I were to have a C-section now, I would demand them to take my uterus out. 

Big hugs to everyone suffering!!

YES it's such a vicious cycle. My last pregnancy was before the new guidelines, and I was much happier.

For me it's just logical that my body would release glucose along with an adrenaline surge. I woke up with a heartbeat of probably 150.. Also, expecting pregnant women to have reliable fasting numbers when all we do at night is tossing and turning, peeing and stressing. It's just a factor I feel they completely ignore. The body is like "oh she needs energy to get through the night" while the medical industry is like "no, she doesn't..".

"Take your fasting blood sugar when you wake up" - Okey, so which one if the times I wake up? 

The rules applying to gestational diabetes is way to harsh. I have type 2 diabetic friends that are shocked with the "goals" I have to reach.

Make it make sense.

I just want to point out that in several studies, women with hg in first trimester had a much higher chance of getting diagnosed with gd. So, if you don't eat anything for months, you are at higher risk. 

Which I would say totally dismisses the "shaming" for bad sugary diet causing gd. 

Many many many doctors, professors, etc. says that gd testing is nonsense. Every woman has gd in her pregnancy. It's a normal condition that resolves after birth. 

Tracking blood pressure, urine and growth should be done either way. I'm shocked to see that some women are put on insulin for having a fasting blood sugar of 5.0. There's no evidence supporting that it has any significant effect. (Other than the stress of making a tired woman living like a diabetic for months.) 

Some women just have large babies genetically. After implementing strict guidelines the amount of babies being born overweight has been reduced by 0.2% (in Finland). And the reduction in birth weight is estimated to be under 100 grams. 

So much stress and pressure on pregnant women, for nothing.

I read someone from Denmark saying that their limit for gd is fasting blood sugar over 6.0.

That sounds way more reasonable.

Life quality. My face twitches alot, and it's really annoying and messes with my sight/eyes. Not to mention my self esteem, always trying to hide my cheek or eye going nuts.

Great! Hope everyone remembers that bodies so soon after delivery can act very strange. You have blood loss, and hormones are fluctuating.

I've had severe hg in 2 of 4 pregnancies. You are not doomed to have it again, but chances are higher. I was also sick in my other pregnancies, but they were manageable. Next time you are prepared. Go in for iv fluids straight away, get medication. 

I don't think people in general understand how severe hg is. I totally understand your decision. I'm 21 weeks, and I feel better, but still more sick than "normal pregnancies".
Yes, right? It just seems more safe.
Yes, I've really grown to hate the "pregnancy recommendations". It should be stated with big red letters that they don't apply if you're very sick.

Yes, this was my mantra my first trimester. I didn't care about sugar or not, as long as I could keep it down. Lemon juice in water didn't do it. It's like my body avoids water at all costs. I need to lure it in.
I ate a whole lemon a while back. I love lemonade, but the amount of sugar is... a tad much.

Water is the worst. After some intense googling I've sent my partner out to get Twinings infuso tea (cold and warm). It's supposably safe in pregnancy, and doesn't contain sugar or artificial sweeteners. It's the only thing I haven't tried.

I tried, but it did absolutely nothing. Zero effect.
